meta:
You are helping me write a single, lean, highly structured prompt that I will copy and paste into Grok to generate professional software requirements.

The prompt you create must:
- Be concise with no unnecessary fluff or preamble
- Instruct Grok to act as an expert product manager and technical architect
- Request these specific sections only:
  1. Executive Summary (3–5 sentences)
  2. User Personas (2–3)
  3. Functional Requirements (as numbered user stories with acceptance criteria)
  4. Non-Functional Requirements (performance, security, scalability, etc.)
  5. Technical Constraints and Assumptions
  6. Out of Scope
  7. Open Questions
- Tell Grok that acceptance criteria should be testable and written in Given/When/Then form
- Tell Grok to label each item in section 5 as a Constraint or an Assumption
- Emphasize precision, completeness, and developer-readiness
- Instruct Grok not to invent facts about the business, users, or content; to flag gaps inline as [AMBIGUITY: …] and to list them under Open Questions with the decision each one blocks
- Instruct Grok to use only the stack and constraints given, and to say so explicitly if it adds an assumption
- Instruct Grok to write so a developer could build and test from the document alone
- Output the finished prompt in a clean code block so I can easily copy it, and include a [PRODUCT IDEA] placeholder (or my idea, if I provided it below) at the end of that prompt

Here is my product idea and any constraints I already know:
[PASTE YOUR IDEA AND CONSTRAINTS]
requirements:
Act as an expert product manager and technical architect. Turn the product idea below into a precise, complete, developer-ready software requirements document. Output only these sections, in this order:

1. Executive Summary: 3–5 sentences.
2. User Personas: 2–3, each with goals, pain points, and context of use.
3. Functional Requirements: numbered user stories ("As a [persona], I want [action] so that [benefit]"), each with testable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form.
4. Non-Functional Requirements: performance, security, privacy, scalability, reliability, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), and maintainability, with measurable targets where possible.
5. Technical Constraints and Assumptions: label each one as a Constraint or an Assumption.
6. Out of Scope
7. Open Questions

Rules:
- Be specific and measurable. No filler, no marketing language, no preamble.
- Do not invent facts about the business, users, or content. When information is missing or ambiguous, mark it inline as [AMBIGUITY: ...] and list it under Open Questions with the decision it blocks.
- Use only the stack and constraints given. If you add an assumption, say so explicitly.
- Write so a developer could build and test from this document alone.

PRODUCT IDEA:
[PRODUCT IDEA]
